name: amdahl_prioritize_by_p
description: Rank optimization candidates by their fraction-of-total-time (P), not by single-kernel win potential; a 10x win on a 1% contributor = 0.9% E2E, a 10% win on a 42% contributor = 4.1% E2E
preconditions: Have a profiled trace with per-kernel total time (duration_avg x occurrences)
Multiple optimization candidates on the table
steps: Compute total_time = duration_avg x occurrences for every kernel
Rank by total_time descending; top-N typically covers 80% of E2E
For each candidate, compute expected E2E speedup via Amdahl: 1 / ((1 - P) + P/S)
Discard any candidate below the bar (e.g. <1% E2E) before investing implementation effort
Only after ranking do you open a tuning ticket for the top contributor
expected_impact: avoids months of work on kernels that can't move E2E by construction; focuses effort on the 2-3 kernels that actually matter
decision_rules: If Amdahl predicts <1% E2E speedup even with a 2x local win, reject the candidate
Decode-phase kernels get priority over prefill for serving workloads (decode is 90-95% of E2E)
